excerpts: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors --> Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors  Ravie Lakshmanan  Nov 03, 2026 Vulnerability / Cyber Attack A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed .

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code.

"SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.

Es handelt sich dabei um eine im August gemeldete und mit Update gestopfte Sicherheitslücke in Simatic-IoT2050-Advanced-Geräten vor Version 4.3.4.1, auf denen Node-RED installiert ist – ein Node.js-basiertes Werkzeug für flussbasierte Programmierung.
Siemens hat mit einer eigenen Sicherheitsmitteilung reagiert und die Version 4.3.4.1 (oder neuer) der Firmware bereitgestellt, die das Problem löst.
CVE-2026-58115 allows unauthenticated access to programming nodes that are capable of executing system commands on the server.
This CVE was assigned by Siemens and affects the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advance, which shows the software is embedded in commercial ICS/OT products.

Our detection for CVE-2026-58115 was published on October 27, and we caught this in-the-wild attempt on October 30, three days later, and moved the CVE into VulnCheck's KEV catalog; it is not in CISA's KEV at the time of writing.

We have seen it hit this Node-RED CVE 16 times between October 30 and November 1, and across our wider canary data the same address has logged 125 hits against 8 different CVEs over recent days: Apache Solr (CVE-2019-17558), Camunda, Gitea, MLflow, Traefik, and Joomla, alongside this Node-RED flaw.
We have since seen 16 events from the same IP against this CVE, covering several different payloads (see the Update section below).

sources.name: BleepingComputer
excerpts: Administrators of affected Zyxel GS1900 switches are advised to install the latest firmware updates to protect against CVE-2026-107441.
Binarly reported its findings to Zyxel on September 29, and the vendor confirmed the new vulnerability on October 11, assigning it CVE-2026-107441.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-107441, is an out-of-bounds write flaw in the switches' web management interface that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to execute operating system commands using specially crafted HTTP requests.
Attacks linked to zero-day flaw On June 16, 2026, Zyxel released security updates addressing CVE-2026-7273, a pre-authentication buffer overflow vulnerability affecting the same GS1900 switches.
When GreyNoise disclosed the campaign on September 21, it attributed the exploitation to CVE-2026-7273, the vulnerability Zyxel had patched in June.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
excerpts: Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel previously said that attackers behind the November incidents exploited the same vulnerability used in October's attacks against French supermarkets.

The French Blood Establishment (Établissement français du sang or EFS), which manages blood collection, processing, and distribution across France, said the incident occurred on November 2 and affected systems used to monitor and control cold-storage chambers.
"No health impact has been identified, and no loss of blood products has been reported," EFS said in its statement [translated from French].
In October, cyberattacks disrupted refrigeration systems at an estimated 250 to 350 French supermarkets, including Intermarché, Carrefour Market, Monoprix, Leclerc, and Super U.
Some refrigeration systems were shut down entirely, while others had their temperature settings changed remotely.

sources.name: The Register
excerpts: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed the incident on Tuesday, saying its own systems had not been directly targeted.
According to reports, attackers changed cold-room temperature settings from -30°C to 110°C.
The latest wave of cold-store attacks comes a month after the first, which affected French supermarket chains Carrefour, Coopérative U, Intermarché, Monoprix, and others.

REG AD "Thus, depending on the circumstances, as soon as the incident occurred, the affected equipment was either brought under control without impacting the products and samples, or neutralized; the products stored in these cold rooms were preventively transferred to other facilities." The EFS did not name the supplier publicly.
That does not mean the equipment or its contents reached the higher temperature.

sources.name: Industrial Cyber
excerpts: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) launched on Monday its 2026 Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month campaign, urging infrastructure owners and operators to strengthen preparedness and improve their ability to withstand and recover from disruptions.

Organizations can participate in Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month with CISA’s toolkit , which includes graphics and plain language text that organizations can use to show the steps they are taking this November to be more resilient.

The Interagency Security Committee offers a wide range of resources to enhance the security of federal government facilities, and CISA’s infrastructure Resilience capabilities, tools, and services are available for exploration.

Local leaders can meet with CISA representatives in their state or district to better understand local infrastructure and the risks it faces, host a town hall meeting to discuss local critical infrastructure issues, and write an opinion editorial in the local paper about the importance of critical infrastructure security and resilience.
Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month empowers American industry, state and local governments, and the Federal Government to each do their part to protect U.S.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two security flaws impacting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog, following active exploitation in the wild.
Ivanti said that, around the time the details were published, it was still working on developing fixes for the local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability exploited in the attack chain.
